INDEPENDENT REVIEW 2 OF 1.24.40'S PDF TOOLS (the mends of review 1) -- 2026-11-25
Build under review: the frozen lantern_1240_r2.html (sha256 ca412c152256c278...), served as index.html, in Chromium
through Playwright. Line numbers below are of that file. Its header still says version: "1.24.39".
"Old" is the committed 1.24.39 page (git show HEAD:site/index.html, sha256 79891e0b...): the working tree's
site/index.html named in the brief had already been rebuilt with the new tools by the time this review ran (it holds
P.redact and stdWidth), so it could not stand for 1.24.39. I wrote none of the code under review and changed nothing
outside this folder.

How it was tried: 34 PDFs made here (make_fixtures.py) by programs that are not Lantern -- reportlab (standard fonts with
no /Widths, AcroForm radio groups and a comb field), pdflatex (Computer Modern, two columns), xelatex (Greek, Cyrillic,
symbols, labels turned 90), LibreOffice (Greek, Cyrillic, a 29-page document), Chromium's own print to PDF (CSS
letter-spacing, word-spacing, rotate(-90deg), writing-mode: vertical-rl, a synthetic italic, a landscape table),
tesseract (a scan with its words), qpdf (linearized, object streams), and pdfw.py here for hand-written drawing programs
(Tc Tw Tz Ts, TJ letter by letter, turned / slanted / mirrored runs, forms nested 1 to 5 deep, a q left open) and file
structures (incremental updates both ways between plain objects and object streams, a hybrid file, an unpacked PDF
attached inside another, 150 bytes of junk before %PDF, offsets 2 bytes off, a table starting at 1, a reused object
number). Every result was read by poppler (pdftotext, -bbox, pdftoppm), qpdf, pypdf, pikepdf and tesseract (eng, rus),
and widths by reportlab's copy of Adobe's AFM tables. cases.json has every check (group, file, check, expected, got,
pass); cases.log the same as text.
  Usage: python3 make_fixtures.py ; python3 run_review.py <new.html> <old.html> <outdir> [groups]
  Groups: afm redact find sweep form helv parse regress layout perf tile text.

COUNTS
  2085 checks, 89 failed (cases.json). By group:
    redact   799 checks, 54 failed  (23 find and area cases on 17 PDFs: marks, poppler/pypdf words, file bytes, picture,
                                     tesseract, words kept and where)
    regress  905 checks,  2 failed  (224 PDFs -- every PDF under tests/fixtures -- opened, read and drawn by 1.24.39
                                     and by this build: page count, words against poppler's, drawing against poppler's)
    sweep    249 checks,  0 failed  (Redact a box on page 1 of every PDF there that opens: no error, no page lost,
                                     qpdf clean)
    afm 13/12, find 16/3, form 12/4, helv 22/2, parse 33/0, layout 13/1, perf 2/0, tile 7/4, text 8/7, harness 6/0
  Of the 89: 4 are the oracle's alone (listed below); 1 is known (Type 3); the rest are items 1-16, most of them
  several checks of one cause (the code-127 bullet alone fails 12 afm checks).
  Usage: python3 make_fixtures.py ; python3 run_review.py <new.html> <old.html> <outdir> [groups] (with no groups it
  writes cases.json; a run of some groups writes cases_<groups>.json and merge_cases.py joins them); about an hour in
  all, most of it the regress and sweep groups. Pictures and the redacted copies named below are in evidence/.

=====================================================================================================================
FAILURES, most serious first  (L = something marked stays readable; I = the copy says something else than the page;
R = regression against 1.24.39; N = new in this round, i.e. worse than the build review 1 tried)
=====================================================================================================================

1. [L] GREEK: A CAPITAL SIGMA AT THE END OF A WORD PUTS THE MARK IN THE WRONG PLACE
   Uppercase Greek ends most surnames and many words in -ΟΣ/-ΑΣ (ΟΔΟΣ = street). "Mark them all" for such a word:
   - on a turned line (a vertical label): one thin box at the line's foot, away from the word; the word stays drawn.
     x_nonlatin.pdf, \rotatebox{90}{ΟΔΟΣ ΕΡΜΟΥ ΤΕΣΣΕΡΑ}: redactMarks(boxes, "οδος") -> [76 529 82 549]; poppler has
     the word at x 71-82, y 459-490 (page space). In the copy 23% of poppler's box for it is black; the same
     through the tile (Redact, Mark them all, Apply, Save: evidence/tile_redact_odos.pdf,
     evidence/greek_vertical_tile_copy.png). Its letters are gone from the copy's words, so only the picture shows it
     -- which is what a reader sees.
   - on a level line: one box over the whole line ([68 677 544 697]): every other word of that line is blacked out and
     taken out of the copy's words (210 bar, και, θερμοκρασία ... on the next line too).
   Smallest reproduction: any run whose text holds "Σ" at a word's end, then redactMarks(boxes, "<any word on it>").
   Cause: PDF_REDACT marksOf: the line is lowercased whole (52822: JavaScript turns Σ at a word's end into ς) but each
   run letter by letter (52826: Σ -> σ), so low.indexOf(t, from) (52827) never finds the run; with no run placed, the
   "whole line, to be safe" box (52841) is built from ln.x0, ln.x1 and ln.y -- for a turned line that is a sliver at
   its first letter. Direction: fold both sides the same way (lowercase the line letter by letter, or map ς to σ
   before comparing); for a line that is not level, build the fallback from its runs' quads, never from x0/x1/y.

2. [L, N] A FORM VALUE OR A TYPED COMMENT IS MARKED AT THE BOTTOM OF THE PAGE; A FIELD WITH NO /AcroForm IS LEFT
   READABLE
   pageText puts a field's value and a typed comment's words in runs with no matrix (49271-49272), and the runs in
   boxes carry neither y nor size (49317), so runBox's fallback (52572) puts their mark at y = 0:
     h_orphan_links.pdf (a filled SSN field, /AP drawn, auto size, no /AcroForm -- a page split from a form):
       redactMarks(boxes, "123-45-6789") -> [358 -6 451 12.5]
     a_annots.pdf (review 1's typed comment ESMERALDA at the top): [297 -6 503 12.5]
   - redact() does not flatten that field (needsFlat 52662-52669 counts neither a form without /Fields nor a widget as
     a comment), draws its appearance into the page picture (pageDraw 50117-50129) and puts the black box at the foot:
     the number stays readable (tesseract reads 123456789; 23% of its box black). The same through the tile
     (evidence/tile_redact_orphan.pdf, evidence/orphan_ssn_tile_copy.png).
   - through the API on an ordinary form or a page with a typed comment, the bogus boxes stay as black bars across the
     page's foot (h_freetext_footer.pdf: [297 -6 523 12] over "Ashcombe Surveying Ltd page 1 of 1"; r_form.pdf: three
     bars from the three filled fields).
   - the viewer's Find (50875, the same marks grouped) highlights a hit in a field or a typed comment at the page foot.
   Review 1's build put these at the top of the comment's rectangle; this is worse. Direction: carry y and size on the
   runs in boxes (or give annotation runs a matrix); flatten widgets whenever there are any, with or without /Fields.

3. [L] A COMB FIELD'S VALUE CANNOT BE FOUND, AND THROUGH THE API IT IS LEFT IN THE COPY
   fillForm(r_form.pdf, {ssn: "987654321"}) then redact with marks from pageText and words ["987654321"]: redact
   flattens the form, the comb draws one digit to a cell, and PDF_TEXT reads "SSN: 9 8 7 6 5 4 3 2 1" (a space
   wherever the pen jumps more than 0.18 of the size, 49302), so finding the words again after flattening (52685)
   finds nothing; the marks given came from the unflattened page and lie at its foot (item 2). The copy shows all nine
   digits (evidence/comb_ssn_copy.png, evidence/redacted_form_find.pdf; pypdf reads them; 8% of poppler's box
   black). In the tile (which flattens first) "Mark them all" says "Not found" while the number is on the page.
   Same cause, item 4.

4. [L] LETTER-SPACED WORDS FROM A BROWSER CANNOT BE FOUND
   Chromium prints CSS letter-spacing by placing each letter itself; Lantern reads "C O N F I D E N T I A L M E R I W E
   A T H E R" (poppler: "CONFIDENTIAL MERIWEATHER"). Mark them all: "Not found"; the API marks nothing and the word
   stays (c_workorder.pdf: 21% of its box black, tesseract reads MERIWEATHER; evidence/meriweather_chrome_copy.png).
   1.24.39 read the line the same way (not a regression of reading), but Redact and the viewer's Find now depend on
   it. Direction: remember which spaces Lantern inserted (a pen jump, not a space letter)
   and let a search match across them, as poppler joins letters whose gaps are even; or join single-letter runs
   whose gaps are equal.

5. [I] SYMBOL AND ZAPFDINGBATS LETTERS ARE DRAWN AS LATIN LETTERS, AND REDACT BURNS THAT INTO THE PAGE
   r_symbol.pdf (Symbol, not embedded, as reportlab, groff, Crystal Reports and old iText write it): the redacted
   page's picture reads "W = 4.7 k, a = 30°, DT < 5 K, m = 0.2" where the page showed "Ω = 4.7 κ, α = 30°, ΔΤ < 5 Κ,
   μ = 0.2" (an ohm sign turned into a W); ZapfDingbats ✔ ✓ ■ became "4 3 n". The same for an Acrobat-made form:
   ticks (ZapfDingbats "4") and radio dots ("l") are drawn "4" and "l" (h_form_zadb.pdf;
   evidence/zapfdingbats_ticks_redacted_copy.png; evidence/symbol_redacted_copy.png against symbol_orig_poppler.png).
   The copy's words say W, k, a, 4. Lantern's viewer already drew them so in 1.24.39; Redact makes it permanent in
   a file that is sent on. Cause: PDF_TEXT font() (49118-49125) reads a standard font without
   /Encoding as WinAnsi, but Symbol and ZapfDingbats have encodings of their own; PDF_DRAW then draws uni(c) in the
   browser's font (49954-49965). Direction: their built-in encodings (glyph names -> Unicode, as for /Differences) and
   their AFM widths, as the 1.24.40 change gave Helvetica and Times.

6. [L, low] WORDS IN FORMS NESTED MORE THAN THREE DEEP ARE DRAWN BUT NOT FOUND
   h_textops.pdf: DEPTHFOUR and DEPTHFIVE (forms 4 and 5 deep) -- Find counts 3 of 5 "depth"; Mark them all misses
   them; tesseract reads them in the copy (19% of their boxes black). PDF_TEXT follows Do to depth 3 (49237),
   PDF_DRAW to 8 (50075). Stamping tools wrap a page in a form each time, so depth grows. Direction: the same limit
   in both (8).

7. [L, low] A LINK NO MARK TOUCHES KEEPS ITS ADDRESS, EVEN WHEN IT HOLDS A WORD LOOKED FOR
   h_orphan_links.pdf: "Open the chart" -> https://records.example.org/patient/WINTERBOURNE/chart is kept on the
   page where WINTERBOURNE was found and marked (52694-52699 keep every untouched link). Direction: drop (or ask
   about) a link on a marked page whose URI or destination holds a word looked for; or say so in Apply's message
   ("bookmarks ... are not changed" already says it for those).

8. [over-redaction] MARKS ARE A FIXED 3 PT WIDER AND TALLER THAN THE LETTERS: NEIGHBOURS ARE CUT AND LOST
   marksOf: pad = 0.3 * (p.size || 10) (52838), but the runs in boxes carry no size (49317), so the pad is always 3 pt;
   with runBox's -0.3 .. +0.95 em the mark of a 10 pt word is 18.5 pt tall. And the 0.5 shrink in invisible() (52630)
   is in text-space units (0.375 pt under Chromium's 0.75 matrix). So at 9-10 pt:
   - the words either side on the same line (a space is 2.5 pt) lose a sliver of a letter and drop out of the copy's
     words: "after" and "fitted" beside "Corrigan" (evidence/marks_neighbours_chrome_copy.png); "Officers", "on" in
     the LaTeX page;
   - at single spacing (leading 1.2-1.25 em) the box clips the descenders of the line above and the tops of the line
     below, and the words under it drop out ("relief valve" under each "Marchetti": 15 words on r_manual2col.pdf;
     evidence/marks_neighbours_manual_copy.png and _orig.png); at leading 1.0 whole words of the line above go
     ("area", "25 m" over "Harrowgate").
   The check "the marks cover no part of a word not looked for" counts these per case.
   Direction: pad relative to the run's own size (p.fs times its matrix), at most the line's leading; a mark from
   the font's ascent to its descent, as Acrobat draws it.

9. [R] A SLANTED OR RAISED RUN IS TAKEN OUT OF ITS LINE (Text Reader, Chat, copy, phrase search)
   c_workorder.pdf (Chromium's synthetic italic for a font with no italic face): "Pump runs fast after Corrigan fitted
   the seal.\nreally" (1.24.39: "Pump runs really fast after ..."); Find "really fast" -> 0. h_textops.pdf: a Tm skew
   "1 0 0.25 1": "Level then Penhaligon end\nOblique"; a run raised 6 pt at 12 pt: "Raised Lockridge\nBelow after".
   Cause: PDF_TEXT's level test (49187) needs m[2] = 0, so a skew (same baseline, same direction) is "not level" and
   49285-49289 put it on a line of its own, sorted after; y0 includes the rise (49173) and lines are grouped within 0.4
   of the size (49291). Direction: decide "level" by the baseline's direction (m[1] = 0, m[0] > 0) only; group by the
   baseline without the rise.

10. FILL IN (THE TILE) CANNOT CHOOSE A RADIO BUTTON
   r_form.pdf, Fill in, tick "Night" (Day was on), Apply, Save: /V /Day, Day still on (evidence/tile_fill_radio.pdf).
   Each button is a check box whose change sets values[groupname] = true/false (52377); fillForm (52091-52095)
   ignores true for a radio group (a value none of the buttons has). Unticking Day turns the whole group off.
   Direction: the tile sends the button's own state name (onOf of its widget), and shows a group's buttons as radios.

11. FILL IN: ACROBAT'S /Opt RADIO GROUPS AND UTF-8 STATE NAMES CANNOT BE FILLED BY THEIR VALUES; P.fields LISTS NO
    CHOICES FOR A RADIO GROUP
   h_form_opt.pdf: a group with states /0 /1 /2 and /Opt (Klein Mittel Größe), as Acrobat writes export values that
   are not plain names: fillForm({size: "Mittel"}) leaves it as it was ("2" works). A group whose states are UTF-8 in
   #xx form (/Gr#C3#BCn): fillForm({colour: "Grün"}) leaves it as it was -- the lexer turns #C3#BC into two Latin-1
   characters (47466), so the state reads "GrÃ¼n". P.fields gives {name, type, value} only, so nobody can learn the
   choices. Direction: read /Opt for buttons; decode a name's bytes as UTF-8 where they are valid UTF-8 (as Acrobat
   and pdf.js show them); list each radio group's choices.

12. A STAMP COMMENT HAS NO /ActualText; MOST LETTERS BEYOND WINANSI ARE DRAWN AS "?"
   addAnnots kind "stamp" (52003-52004) draws Y.lit(codes) without typed(): poppler reads "R = 4.7 KOHM <= 5 %, ?P >=
   2 BAR, ?????? ?? ?? OK" for "R = 4.7 kΩ ≤ 5 %, Δp ≥ 2 bar, Привет 中文 😀 ok". Edit text, a text box, a field and
   P.stamp do carry it, and poppler reads every letter back from them (the emoji as a surrogate pair). Only ten signs
   are spelled out (SAY, 50406); Greek other than Ω, Cyrillic, Chinese and emoji are drawn "?" -- searchable, but a
   person sees "??????". Worth saying in the tool when it happens.

13. [minor] WINANSI CODE 127 (A BULLET) IS READ AS A CONTROL CHARACTER AND MEASURED AS "?"
   The standard's WinAnsi table maps the unused codes (127, 129, 141, 143, 144, 157) to the bullet; reportlab writes
   every "•" as \177 and poppler shows a bullet. Lantern reads U+007F (uni(), 49118-49125), draws nothing, and gives
   it the width of "?" (556 Helvetica, 444 Times) instead of 350: the words after it sit 1.85 pt to the right at 9 pt
   (a mark for "918-555-0199" starts 1.56 pt right of poppler's). After Redact the bullet is gone from the picture and
   the copy's words hold U+007F. Every other WinAnsi width of Helvetica, Helvetica-Bold, Times-Roman/Bold/Italic/
   BoldItalic, "Arial,Bold" and "TimesNewRomanPS-BoldItalicMT" equals Adobe's AFM (219 letters each).

14. [minor] THE EXTRA FONTS FOR NON-WINANSI LETTERS HAVE NO /ToUnicode
   Poppler decodes their /uniXXXX glyph names, so Greek and Cyrillic come back as themselves (checked on xelatex,
   LibreOffice and Chromium pages); pypdf 6.0 does not, and returns "/uni03A4/uni03B5/uni03C7..." for every such
   letter of a redacted page (pypdf's limitation -- the oracle -- but a ToUnicode CMap, 52723-52728, would make every
   reader agree; pypdf is what many text pipelines use).

15. [minor] SLANTED TEXT: THE MARK IS THE BOX ROUND THE WORD'S FOUR CORNERS
   A word at 30 degrees gets an upright box that covers parts of its neighbours ("degree", "line" beside "Montague";
   "TYP" beside "OBADIAH"). Inherent in marks that are rectangles (Acrobat's are quads); worth knowing.

16. [minor] TURNING THE PHONE DOES NOT REFIT THE PAGES
   Opened at 844 x 390, then 390 x 844: no sideways scroll of the page itself, but the first page stays 556 px wide in
   a 390 px window (it scrolls inside the page area). Opening at 390 or 360 wide fits (passes).

KNOWN (told by the coordinator): a Type 3 font's letters are drawn ten times too far apart (PDF_DRAW 49969 multiplies
by FontMatrix[0] again). Seen here as the one drawing regression: review 1's t_type3.pdf, mean grey difference from
poppler 0.86 against 1.24.39's 0.19.

=====================================================================================================================
CHECKS THAT FAILED BECAUSE THE ORACLE WAS WRONG (said plainly)
=====================================================================================================================
 - "night shift" in c_workorder.pdf: poppler's plain text breaks that line (CSS word-spacing), so it counts 0; Lantern's 1
   is right.
 - Two "stray mark" checks (title_find, ops_find): the marks are on OBADIAH (30 degrees) and on the mirrored "Quenby",
   which poppler cannot put in a box (it reads "ybneuQ"); the marks are where the words are.
 - Slanted (30 degree) lines: poppler groups slanted letters into different "words" in the copy, where each letter has
   its own Tm ("0T" for "0", "TY"); the letters are where they were and -raw reads "R 450 TYP OBADIAH" in both. The
   "kept words" checks of title_* and ops_find count these.
 - "Waverley" read by tesseract in latex_find: the second one is hyphenated across lines ("Wa-" / "verley's"); neither
   poppler nor Lantern sees it as the word.
 - The title block's Symbol line: poppler here has no Symbol font and shows "■" for some letters; its words are not a
   fair "expected" there (item 5 stands on r_symbol.pdf, where poppler reads Ω κ α).
 - pypdf: no uniXXXX names (item 14) and it drops spaces between letters written one at a time ("Servicereport").
 - pdf_review2_1239/ve_cycle.pdf (an optional-content cycle): poppler loops forever on it; Lantern opens and draws it.
   The harness now stops any tool after 120 s.
 - Letter-spaced lines (Tc 4, Tz 150 in r_invoice.pdf): poppler splits them into single letters; Lantern drops a whole
   word when a mark reaches any of its letters, so a few letters counted "lost" in inv_find are by the rule (the mark
   that reached them is item 8's).
 - A first OCR check matched pieces shared with other words (Kestrel-5 beside Kestrel-3, DEPTHTWO beside DEPTHTHREE) and
   joined OCR words; and a first ink check counted dark pixels, which unmarked black text also has. Both were mended
   before the runs in cases.json.

=====================================================================================================================
WHAT PASSED
=====================================================================================================================
Redaction (poppler, pypdf, the file's bytes unpacked, the picture and tesseract all agree the word is gone):
 - Level words in Helvetica, Helvetica-Bold, Times-Roman/Italic/Bold/BoldItalic and Courier with no /Widths; with Tc 4,
   Tw 14, Tz 150 and 200, Ts 4 and 9 (a raised word: the mark is where it is drawn, review 1's ZEPHYRINE case); a number
   found by part of it ("555-0143" took "918-555-0143" whole); Latin-1 letters (Þórsdóttir); TJ letter by letter; a
   run at 2x and at 0.5x; two columns; justified text.
 - Turned and odd runs: labels at 90 and 270 degrees, upside down, mirrored, a matrix skew, 30 degrees; a form XObject
   placed level and turned 90; forms nested to depth 3; Chromium's rotate(-90deg) and writing-mode: vertical-rl
   (one letter a Tj, joined into one line as the mend says); xelatex Greek and Cyrillic, level and turned 90 (words
   with no capital sigma at their end); LibreOffice Greek and Cyrillic; tesseract's scan.
 - Pages with a CropBox, turned 90 / 180 / 270 with a crop, a MediaBox at 100 200: every target black where poppler
   shows it; a word wholly outside the seen box (OUTSIDERWORD) not written into the copy's words; of a word across the
   crop's edge only the part inside kept; every page keeps its turn and seen box.
 - A q left open with a clip and a cm, a second content stream, more Q than q, a form that leaves a cm: drawn as
   poppler draws it (mean grey difference 0.19) and redacted cleanly.
 - Filled text fields (not comb) and an Acrobat-style check box form: the values flattened, found and gone.
 - Words kept: on every case without a cause above, every word away from the marks is found again by poppler, split as
   poppler split the original, within 4 pt along its line; every Greek, Cyrillic or
   symbol word kept (Ω ≤ ≥ ° ± µ √ → ∑) reads as itself in poppler.
 - Robustness: 249 PDFs (every one in tests/fixtures that opens) redacted with a box on page 1: none threw, none lost a
   page, every copy qpdf-clean.
Reading (PDF_TEXT) against 1.24.39: 224 PDFs, 341 pages: words as near poppler's or nearer on all but h_textops.pdf
 (item 9); nearer on t_chrome.pdf (0.74 -> 0.89), fonts_web.pdf (0.73 -> 1.00) and c_workorder.pdf -- Chromium's
 sideways labels now read as words. Drawing: the same, or nearer poppler, on 339 of 340 pages (the one is Type 3).
Adobe's metrics: every WinAnsi letter's width but code 127 equals the AFM for Helvetica, Helvetica-Bold,
 Helvetica-Oblique, Times-Roman/Bold/Italic/BoldItalic, "Arial,Bold", "TimesNewRomanPS-BoldItalicMT"; Courier-Bold 600.
PDF_PARSE: an incremental update with a classic table; an xref-stream update over an object-stream file whose new page
 dictionary stands alone (the newer plain copy wins); a plain file updated with the new page in an object stream (the
 stream wins over the older plain copy); a hybrid file (classic table + /XRefStm, the packed objects only in the stream,
 as Word writes it); linearized files (plain and with object streams); an unpacked PDF attached inside another (plain
 and with object streams: the outer document only); 150 bytes before %PDF; every offset 2 bytes off; a table starting
 at 1; a number freed and reused at generation 1 -- all read as poppler reads them, and a stamped copy keeps the
 newest page. 1.24.39 (git HEAD) reads them all the same way already (its PDF_PARSE had the cross-reference chain).
 LibreOffice's 29-page document: drawn in 404 ms against 389 (and 327 against 360 with object streams) -- no
 slower, but this document did not show the slowness the mend was for, so the gain is not confirmed.
Fill in: a radio value ('Night'), a group none was on ('Card'), a value none of the buttons has (left as it was), ""
 and "Off" (all off, /V /Off), a state name of an /Opt group ("2"), a comb drawn one digit to a 20 pt cell -- all
 through the API.
Words Helvetica cannot draw: Edit text, a text box comment, a field and P.stamp: drawn "Ohm", "<=", ">="; poppler reads
 Ω ≤ ≥ Δ, Привет, 中文 back through /ActualText (the emoji as a surrogate pair); the field's /V is the text as typed; a
 stamp of WinAnsi words only has no /ActualText and reads as typed.
Layout: the tile at 390 x 844 (a landscape table, an 11 x 17 drawing), 360 x 740 and 844 x 390: no sideways scroll,
 the first page fitted to the width, no page errors.
The tile: Redact (Mark them all, Apply, Save) on a vertical Latin label (NIGHTJAR) and the level ΟΔΟΣ: black.

=====================================================================================================================
NOT TESTED
=====================================================================================================================
 - Acrobat or Adobe Reader themselves, Word-made PDFs (hybrid files were made by hand as Word writes them), Firefox,
   Safari, Android; Greek OCR (no Greek for tesseract here: the Greek leak is shown by the picture check alone).
 - Redaction at other than 200 dpi; very large pages (maxSide 5000); encrypted PDFs through redact (review 1 did).
 - Remove hidden, Protect, Reduce size, Combine, Compare, Export (not among the mends).
